scope: Proposal only. No package archive or key material was downloaded or imported; no verifier was run; no package closure, image, or worker is established.

snapshot.db_signature_note: DB bytes are hash-pinned before and after use. A supplied DB signature must verify. Hashes of DB-embedded PGPSIG bytes are not independent authenticity pins; the actual archive signature check is still required.

arch_master_policy.temporal_limit: Current page observed on 2026-10-25; not an archival capture proving the same set on 2026-09-30.
arch_master_policy.threshold: At least 3 valid certifications from 3 distinct pinned master keys out of these 5. The official Arch page says package maintainer keys should have at least three master-key signatures.
arch_master_policy.material_rule: Fetch only material from a source linked by the official Arch page; require exact full primary fingerprint below. Preserve material/source metadata and validate owner signatures, certifications, expiry, and designated revocations with an accepted verifier. Keyserver listings alone are not verification. No key bytes have been fetched or checked.

bootstrap_signer.name: Christian Hesse
bootstrap_signer.certification_status: Observed keyserver listings and current official Arch page only; no certificate/signature bytes were cryptographically verified.
required_checks: Verify at least three distinct pinned-master certifications.
Validate any signing subkey binding and its validity at signature time.
Check signer, subkey, certification expiry and designated revocations at signature time and before acceptance.
Reject unknown primary fingerprints, invalid/missing certification paths, expired-at-signature keys, or applicable revocations.

pacman.signer_expectation: Christian Hesse is only a candidate based on the DB packager field. The current package page is -3 and does not prove the exact -2 signer; inspect and verify the exact archived signature before extraction.

signature_policy.db_signature_rule: Optional only as pinned; exact DB hashes remain mandatory before and after use; verify a DB signature if supplied.
signature_policy.signer_expectation_limit: Christian Hesse is the expected signer for the keyring package based on its official page, and a candidate signer for pacman based only on metadata. The exact archived pacman -2 signature has not been observed or verified. If its verified signature names another primary key, stop and require separate review before accepting it.
signature_policy.subkey_rule: Allow a signing subkey only when its binding to the accepted primary key verifies and it is valid at signature time.
signature_policy.certification_threshold: 3 distinct valid certifications among the 5 pinned master fingerprints.
signature_policy.revocation_expiry_rule: Validate signer, subkey, certifications and masters at signature time. Reject invalid, expired-at-signature, unbound, or applicable-revoked material; recheck designated revokers before acceptance.
signature_policy.time_rule: Reject package signatures later than 2026-09-30T23:59:59Z or outside key validity. For archlinux-keyring require consistency with the official page's 2026-09-09T07:47:00Z time. Packet time is not an independent trusted timestamp.
signature_policy.trustdb_rule: Use isolated disposable key data and only the explicit five-master allowlist. No ambient keyrings, keyserver refresh, trust-all, TOFU, or automatic import. Do not trust every key shipped in archlinux-keyring.
signature_policy.pgpsig_rule: The DB PGPSIG digest is not an independent trust pin; verify the fetched detached signature over the exact archive and record its digest only after it is bound to that row.

verifier_candidate.observed_by: Parent-agent read-only host inspection; not independently reverified in this phase.
verifier_candidate.trust_boundary: Authenticated Ubuntu APT metadata would establish Ubuntu package origin, not Arch package trust. Arch package signatures still require the separate pinned Arch chain.
unproven: Exact signed Ubuntu InRelease/Packages, package stanza and .deb archive are not retained or verified.
Installed gpgv bytes are not bound to an authenticated package payload; Ubuntu keyring file is not bound to its authenticated package payload.
APT source configuration and insecure/unauthenticated overrides are not captured and audited.
gpgv alone does not establish Arch certification/revocation paths; an authenticated certificate-audit method is not pinned.
No verifier was run on Arch key or package data.
acceptance_requirements: Authenticate the exact Ubuntu InRelease and Packages chain using the Ubuntu archive-key fingerprints above.
Bind the exact gpgv .deb and installed binary hash, and the archive-keyring .deb and installed keyring hash, to authenticated package metadata.
Audit APT source and config for Trusted=yes, AllowUnauthenticated, AllowInsecureRepositories, AllowDowngradeToInsecureRepositories, or equivalent bypasses.
Pin an authenticated certificate/revocation audit capability as well as detached-signature verification.
Obtain SOL read-only acceptance before Stage A.
verifier_candidate.ubuntu_security_doc_note: Ubuntu documentation explains signed APT archive metadata and warns that Trusted=yes and allow-unauthenticated/insecure settings disable verification.

other_verifier_candidates.decision: Unresolved; located integrity page lists an expired code-signing certificate and does not establish a current 2026 installer signer pin.

preconditions: SOL approves signer/master chain, verifier provenance, policy, and exact rows.
Verifier and certificate-audit tool are independently authenticated and binary-bound.
Pinned key material passes fingerprint, certification, expiry, and designated-revocation checks.
Archive filename, size, and SHA match pinned DB row.
Keyring package signature passes before extraction or key import; extraction is bounded and isolated.

review: exact usr/bin/vercmp hash, mode, ELF identity and dependencies
stage_b.rule: Do not execute vercmp until separate review accepts its exact identity/dependencies. Do not bulk-download closure packages until an independent recomputation from both hash-pinned DBs is reviewed and accepted.
